blogs.title: When Anaphylaxis Keeps Coming Back: Making Sense of Multiphasic Reactions
blogs.description: A deep dive into biphasic and multiphasic anaphylaxis - what we actually know about incidence rates, why predicting who will relapse remains frustratingly difficult, and how to approach management when your patient keeps crashing despite 'adequate' treatment. The case highlights the unsettling reality that evidence-based guidance for multiphasic courses is virtually nonexistent.

blogs.title: The 0.3mg Problem: Why Your Epinephrine Auto-Injector May Be Underdosing Adults
blogs.description: This case exposes a practical dosing gap that many clinicians overlook - adult auto-injectors often deliver only 0.3mg when guidelines recommend 0.5mg. Explore the evidence linking underdosing to treatment escalation, why auto-injectors remain popular despite this limitation, and practical strategies to ensure your patients get the dose they actually need.

blogs.title: Steroids in Anaphylaxis: Killing the Sacred Cow
blogs.description: For decades, corticosteroids have been standard anaphylaxis adjuncts, prescribed to 'prevent biphasic reactions.' But mounting evidence shows no benefit - and potential harm. This post examines why steroid use persists despite guideline changes, the data driving the paradigm shift, and how to change your practice when tradition conflicts with evidence.

blogs.title: Beyond the Allergen: When to Suspect Systemic Mastocytosis
blogs.description: Severe or atypical anaphylaxis may be the first clue to an underlying mast cell disorder. This case illustrates how elevated tryptase, hepatomegaly, and neuropsychiatric symptoms can point toward systemic mastocytosis - even when formal diagnostic criteria aren't met. Learn when to broaden your differential beyond simple IgE-mediated allergy.

blogs.title: The Tryptase Tango: Getting Your Timing Right
blogs.description: Proper tryptase sampling is critical for both confirming anaphylaxis and detecting underlying mast cell disease - yet it's frequently mishandled in busy emergency settings. This practical guide covers the ideal sampling intervals, common pitfalls, and why getting this right matters for your patient's long-term diagnostic workup.

blogs.title: How Long is Long Enough? The Observation Time Dilemma
blogs.description: Guidelines conflict, evidence is thin, and the stakes are high. This post navigates the controversy over observation periods after anaphylaxis, reviewing risk-stratified approaches like the UK three-tier model and offering a practical framework for balancing patient safety against healthcare resource utilization in the ED.
